items.title: Tom Lellis interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, July 31, 2007
items.q: I thought Reagan split up the — in fact I thought Reagan began the entire whole rap movement

ctx.x: Your Bush league. You’re talking about your Bush league. I’m making an educated guess that you’re not too happy with the current state of affairs.

Yeah I think it’s the greatest travesty this country has endured. I thought Nixon was bad, I thought Reagan split up the — in fact I thought Reagan began the entire whole rap movement and all that when he said, I don’t think he was necessarily racist I just think that he said if you don’t have money I’m sorry, I can’t deal with you. And so that took a lot of people and just put them out of society’s flow. And then this guy came along, and he has rewritten all the rules or broken all the rules I think. He is a…

and the bottom said “C-O-U de etat. Because that’s what I think we’ve endured. I think the Supreme Court vote that took one vote to change the national election — you know I just read in the Times that it’s within the Constitution with a majority of Congress they can change the number of Supreme Court justices and it’s been down to five and as high as eleven.
